newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Asian MTBE - Direction sought from Bangchak tender.
newsitem.headline: Asian MTBE - Direction sought from Bangchak tender.

text.p: Asian spot MTBE prices held steady in lacklustre trade as the market sought direction from Thai refiner Bangchak Petroleum Plc's import tender for April, industry sources said on Wednesday.
Producers were offering free-on-board (fob) Singapore MTBE lifting April at around $270-$272 per tonne, but "nobody's asking for cargoes", a trader said.
Last week, end March-early April MTBE was being assessed in a wide range of between $268-$275 per tonne fob, with trade heard as high at $275.
"There is no direction from Singapore because there is no business," said a trader. "The direction of the market will be reflected in Bangchak's tender today."
Bangchak is seeking 1,5000 tonnes of MTBE for second-half April delivery in a tender closing and valid on Wednesday.
In its last tender, Bangchak bought its March requirement from Saudi Basic Industries Corp (SABIC) at $280-$285 per tonne c-and-f.
"The last time the award was in the low $280s. If it is awarded in the low $270s, then $270 fob Singapore does not work," a trader said.
"Prices are heading southwards...I don't know how much, it depends on how keen the producers are to sell," he said.
Traders were still concerned on a potential build in stocks in Singapore.
"The US Gulf and Europe are overstocked, plus the new Sadaf plant is starting exports... there is no choice but for Middle East cargoes to head here," a trader said.
The 700,000-tonne-per-year Sadaf plant, 50:50 joint-venture between SABIC and the Royal Dutch Shell is due to startup in March/April.
